questions.prompt: Neurons carry electrical signals from body parts to the brain.
questions.explanation: Neurons are specialised cells that transmit electrical signals between the body and the brain.

questions.prompt: Which TWO organs are part of the digestive system?

questions.prompt: Light bends when it passes from air into water.
questions.explanation: Light changes speed when entering a different material, which causes it to bend. This is called refraction.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Describe how light bends at material boundaries

questions.prompt: What property of a sound wave determines how high or low the pitch sounds?

visuals.altText: Bar chart comparing pitch of four sounds: bass drum low pitch at 80 Hz, guitar medium pitch at 440 Hz, whistle high pitch at 2000 Hz, dog whistle very high pitch at 23000 Hz

questions.explanation: Frequency is how many vibrations occur each second. Higher frequency gives a higher pitch; lower frequency gives a lower pitch.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Identify what determines pitch

questions.prompt: A louder sound has a greater amplitude than a quieter sound.
questions.explanation: Amplitude measures the size of the vibrations. Larger vibrations transfer more energy, which we hear as louder sound.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Understand relationship between amplitude and volume

questions.prompt: Which TWO actions make a solid dissolve faster in water?

visuals.altText: Table showing time for salt to dissolve under different conditions: still cold water 120 seconds, stirred cold water 60 seconds, still warm water 45 seconds, stirred warm water 20 seconds

questions.explanation: Stirring moves fresh water past the solid surface. Heating gives water particles more energy to break apart the solid.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Identify factors that affect dissolving rate

questions.prompt: Which part of the brain controls balance and coordination?

visuals.altText: Table listing four brain structures and their functions: cerebrum handles thinking and memory, cerebellum controls balance and coordination, brain stem manages breathing and heartbeat, spinal cord carries signals between brain and body

rows: Carries signals to and from the body

questions.explanation: The cerebellum, located at the back of the brain, coordinates muscle movements and maintains balance.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Identify brain regions and their roles

questions.prompt: In a gas, the particles are tightly packed together.
questions.explanation: Gas particles are far apart and move freely. Solids have tightly packed particles; liquids have particles close together but able to slide past each other.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Describe particle arrangement in gases

questions.prompt: Match each seed type to how it is dispersed.

rows: Light and fluffy, carried by wind
Have hooks that stick to fur

questions.prompt: Put the stages of a frog life cycle in order from first to last.
questions.explanation: A frog begins as an egg, hatches into a tadpole that breathes with gills, develops legs to become a froglet, and matures into an adult frog with lungs.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Order the stages of a frog life cycle

questions.prompt: A thermometer reads 25 degrees Celsius in the morning. By afternoon it reads 38 degrees Celsius. What is the temperature rise?

visuals.altText: Number line from 20 to 40 degrees Celsius with marks at 25 and 38 highlighted to show the temperature rise

questions.explanation: The temperature rise is found by subtracting the morning reading from the afternoon reading: 38 minus 25 equals 13 degrees Celsius.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Calculate temperature change

questions.prompt: What happens when white light passes through a glass prism?

options.text: It disappears completely from view entirely
It turns a deep shade of blue
It splits into a spectrum of colours

visuals.altText: Line graph showing the spectrum of visible light from red at 700 nm wavelength through orange, yellow, green, blue, to violet at 400 nm wavelength, demonstrating how a prism separates white light

questions.explanation: A prism refracts different colours of light by different amounts because each colour has a different wavelength. This spreads white light into the visible spectrum.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Describe what happens to white light in a prism

questions.prompt: A seed will germinate and grow into a plant even if it is given no water.
questions.explanation: Seeds need water, suitable temperature, and oxygen to germinate. Without water, the embryo inside the seed cannot begin to grow.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Identify conditions needed for seed germination

questions.prompt: A bass drum produces a deep, low sound. The drum skin vibrates...

options.text: At a high rate of speed

questions.explanation: A low-pitched sound is produced by slow vibrations, which means a low frequency. The bass drum vibrates fewer times per second than a high-pitched instrument.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Relate pitch to vibration frequency

questions.prompt: Order the stages when ice is heated until it becomes steam, from first to last.

visuals.altText: Number line from minus 20 to 120 degrees Celsius showing key temperature points: 0 degrees C marked as melting point of ice and 100 degrees C marked as boiling point of water

questions.explanation: Ice (solid) melts at 0 degrees C into liquid water. As heating continues, the water warms until it boils at 100 degrees C and becomes water vapour (gas/steam).

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Order the stages of heating ice to steam

questions.prompt: Which TWO are examples of renewable energy sources?

options.text: Burning coal in a power station

questions.explanation: Solar and wind energy are renewable because sunlight and wind are naturally replenished. Coal, natural gas, and petroleum are fossil fuels that take millions of years to form and are non-renewable.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Identify renewable energy sources

questions.prompt: In which type of circuit does each bulb have its own separate branch?

visuals.altText: Table comparing series and parallel circuits: in a series circuit components share one path and if one bulb breaks all go out; in a parallel circuit each component has its own branch and if one bulb breaks the others stay lit

questions.explanation: In a parallel circuit, each component has its own branch connected to the power source. If one bulb breaks, the others remain lit because current still flows through their branches.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Distinguish between series and parallel circuits

questions.prompt: Camouflage helps animals blend into their surroundings to avoid predators.
questions.explanation: Camouflage is an adaptation where an animal's colour or pattern matches its environment, making it harder for predators or prey to detect.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Explain how camouflage helps survival

questions.prompt: Which type of weather front brings heavy rain and a sudden drop in temperature?

visuals.altText: Table comparing weather fronts: warm front brings gradual warming and light rain, cold front brings heavy rain and sudden temperature drop, stationary front brings prolonged cloudy weather, high pressure brings clear skies

questions.explanation: A cold front occurs when cold air pushes under warm air. The warm air rises rapidly, cools, and forms tall clouds that produce heavy rain and a sudden drop in temperature.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Identify weather patterns associated with fronts

questions.prompt: Match each heat transfer method to the correct example.

visuals.altText: Table showing three heat transfer methods: conduction transfers heat through direct contact like touching a hot spoon, convection transfers heat through fluid movement like hot air rising, radiation transfers heat through waves like sunlight warming skin

rows: Hot air rising from a heater

questions.explanation: Conduction transfers heat through direct contact between particles. Convection occurs when heated fluids (liquids or gases) move. Radiation transfers heat as electromagnetic waves through space.

metadata.skill: Match heat transfer methods to examples

questions.prompt: Order the steps of a fair test investigation from first to last.

visuals.altText: Table listing five steps of scientific investigation in order: first ask a testable question, then make a prediction or hypothesis, next plan a fair test changing only one variable, then collect and record data, finally draw a conclusion based on evidence

questions.explanation: Scientific investigations begin with a question, followed by a prediction. A fair test is planned (changing one variable at a time), data is collected, and finally a conclusion is drawn from the evidence.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Order the steps of a fair test investigation

questions.prompt: A stick insect looks exactly like a twig on a tree. This adaptation is called...
questions.explanation: Mimicry is when an animal copies the appearance of another object or organism. A stick insect copying a twig's shape is mimicry. Camouflage is blending into the background, not copying a specific object.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Distinguish mimicry from camouflage

questions.prompt: Viruses and bacteria are both types of microorganisms.
questions.explanation: Microorganisms are living things too small to see without a microscope. Bacteria are single-celled organisms. Viruses are even smaller particles that need a host cell to reproduce.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Classify types of microorganisms

questions.prompt: Which TWO methods can separate a mixture of sand and water?

options.text: Using a sieve to sort grains

visuals.altText: Bar chart showing the effectiveness of five separation methods for a sand-water mixture: filtration 95 percent effective, evaporation 100 percent effective, magnetic separation 0 percent, sieving 10 percent, freezing 5 percent

questions.explanation: Filtration traps sand on the filter paper while water passes through. Evaporation removes the water, leaving dry sand behind. Sand is not magnetic, so magnetic separation does not work.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Select methods to separate mixtures

questions.prompt: Match each body system to its main function.
questions.explanation: The respiratory system handles breathing and gas exchange. The circulatory system pumps blood. The nervous system sends signals to control the body. The skeletal system supports and protects organs.

metadata.skill: Match body systems to their functions

questions.prompt: Why do polar bears have a thick layer of blubber under their skin?

options.text: It insulates their body and traps heat
It makes them invisible to predators
It stores oxygen for breathing underwater

visuals.altText: Bar chart showing polar bear adaptations and their survival benefits: thick blubber provides 10 cm insulation rated high benefit, white fur provides camouflage rated high benefit, large paws provide swimming ability rated medium benefit, small ears reduce heat loss rated medium benefit

questions.explanation: Blubber is a thick layer of fat that acts as insulation, trapping body heat in the freezing Arctic environment. This is essential for survival in temperatures below zero.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Explain polar bear adaptations

questions.prompt: Order the organisms to show the correct flow of energy in a food chain, starting from the original energy source.

visuals.altText: Pie chart showing energy distribution in a food chain: sun provides 100 percent energy, grass captures 10 percent through photosynthesis, rabbit gets 1 percent from eating grass, fox gets 0.1 percent from eating rabbit, illustrating energy loss at each level

questions.explanation: Energy flows from the Sun to producers (grass), then to primary consumers (rabbit), then to secondary consumers (fox). Energy decreases at each step as organisms use most of it for life processes.

metadata.skill: Order organisms to show energy flow

questions.prompt: Match each material to its key property.

visuals.altText: Table showing material hardness on Mohs scale: diamond rated 10 as hardest natural material, copper rated 3 as good electrical conductor, glass rated 5.5 as transparent and brittle, rubber rated variable as flexible and elastic

questions.explanation: Diamond is the hardest natural material. Copper conducts electricity well. Glass is transparent but breaks easily. Rubber stretches and returns to its original shape.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Match materials to their properties

questions.prompt: Which process carries small rock particles away from their original location?

visuals.altText: Bar chart comparing rates of earth processes over one year: weathering breaks down 2 mm of rock, erosion moves 5 mm of particles, deposition deposits 3 mm of sediment, compaction reduces layer thickness by 1 mm

questions.explanation: Erosion is the process that transports weathered rock particles away from their original location. Weathering breaks rocks down, but erosion moves the pieces.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Distinguish erosion from weathering and deposition

questions.prompt: A student dissolves 30 grams of salt in water. It takes 6 minutes to fully dissolve. How many grams dissolve per minute?
questions.explanation: Divide the total mass dissolved by the time taken: 30 grams divided by 6 minutes equals 5 grams per minute.

metadata.skill: Calculate dissolving rate from data

questions.prompt: Order the stages in the formation of a rainstorm, from first to last.
questions.explanation: Warm moist air rises and expands. As it rises, it cools and water vapour condenses into tiny droplets. These droplets gather to form clouds. When droplets become heavy enough, rain falls.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Order the stages of rainstorm formation

questions.prompt: A metal spoon and a wooden spoon are left in hot soup. After five minutes, which spoon handle will feel hotter?

options.text: The metal spoon, as metal conducts heat well
The wooden spoon, as wood holds heat much better

visuals.altText: Line graph showing temperature at spoon handle over 5 minutes: metal spoon handle rises from 22 degrees C to 45 degrees C steadily, wooden spoon handle rises from 22 degrees C to 26 degrees C slowly

questions.explanation: Metal is a good conductor of heat, so heat travels quickly from the hot soup up the handle. Wood is a poor conductor (an insulator), so the handle stays closer to room temperature.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Compare thermal conductivity of materials

questions.prompt: Five students measure the length of a table. Their results are: 120 cm, 122 cm, 119 cm, 121 cm, 118 cm. What is the range of these measurements?
questions.explanation: The range is the difference between the largest and smallest measurements. The largest is 122 cm and the smallest is 118 cm, so the range is 122 minus 118 equals 4 cm.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Calculate the range of measurements

questions.prompt: What pattern do magnetic field lines form around a bar magnet?

options.text: Curved lines from north pole to south pole
Circular loops around the centre and edges only

visuals.altText: Table of magnetic field observations: near north pole iron filings form curved lines spreading outward, at centre lines run parallel along the magnet length, near south pole lines curve inward converging, between two opposite poles lines connect directly

questions.explanation: Magnetic field lines form curved patterns that emerge from the north pole, loop through space, and enter the south pole. They never cross and are closest together near the poles where the field is strongest.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Describe magnetic field line patterns

questions.prompt: Match each variable type to its correct example in a plant growth experiment testing different soils.

visuals.altText: Table defining variable types in a plant growth experiment: independent variable is what you change which is the soil type, dependent variable is what you measure which is plant height, control variable is what you keep the same which is the amount of water given daily

questions.explanation: The independent variable is what the investigator changes (soil type). The dependent variable is what is measured (plant height). Control variables are kept the same to ensure a fair test (amount of water).

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Classify types of experimental variables

questions.prompt: A car travels 240 kilometres using 20 litres of fuel. How many kilometres per litre does the car achieve?
questions.explanation: Divide the total distance by the fuel used: 240 km divided by 20 litres equals 12 kilometres per litre.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Calculate rate from experimental data

questions.instructions: Write just the number, without the unit.

questions.prompt: The bar chart shows plant growth with different water amounts: Plant A received 100 mL and grew 12 cm, Plant B received 200 mL and grew 18 cm, Plant C received 300 mL and grew 15 cm, Plant D received 400 mL and grew 8 cm. Which plant grew the tallest?

visuals.altText: Bar chart showing plant height for four plants with different water amounts: Plant A received 100 mL water and grew 12 cm tall, Plant B received 200 mL and grew 18 cm, Plant C received 300 mL and grew 15 cm, Plant D received 400 mL and grew 8 cm

questions.explanation: Plant B grew to 18 cm, which is taller than Plant A (12 cm), Plant C (15 cm), and Plant D (8 cm). This shows that giving the most water does not always produce the tallest plant.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Read and compare data from a bar chart

questions.prompt: Which THREE factors should be kept the same when testing how different soils affect plant growth?

options.text: The amount of water each plant receives
The amount of sunlight each plant receives
The height of each plant after a week

visuals.altText: Pie chart showing the relative importance of controlling variables in a plant experiment: amount of water 25 percent, amount of sunlight 25 percent, seed type 20 percent, pot size 15 percent, room temperature 15 percent, soil type is the variable being tested and should not be controlled

questions.explanation: The soil type is the independent variable being tested, so it must differ between groups. Water, sunlight, and seed type are control variables that must stay the same. Plant height is the dependent variable that is measured, not controlled.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Identify control variables in an investigation

questions.prompt: In an experiment testing how light affects plant growth, which factor is a control variable?

options.text: The amount of light each plant receives
The amount of water given to each plant
The final height of each plant
The number of leaves on each plant

questions.explanation: The control variable is what is kept the same. The amount of light is the independent variable (what is changed), the plant height and leaf count are dependent variables (what is measured), and the water amount should be kept constant as a control variable.

metadata.subject: science
metadata.skill: Distinguish independent, dependent, and control variables
